item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q000_runtime","answer":"The first SCOPe pass already pins down the taxonomy shift: in release 2.04, 1nqd’s ColG collagen-binding domain was in fold b.23 while Cry3A’s C-terminal domain was in b.18; in current SCOPe, 1nqd has been moved into b.18. I’m drilling one level deeper now to distinguish the fold/superfamily/family relationship instead of letting a shared beta-class label do too much work.","evidence_used":[]}]}

item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.04 the ColG collagenase collagen-binding domain from 1nqd and the Cry3A C-terminal domain from 1dlc were only in the same class, not in the same fold: 1nqd chain A d1nqda_ and chain B d1nqdb_ were b.23.2.1, Collagen-binding domain family, in the Collagen-binding domain superfamily of the CUB-like fold b.23, whereas the Cry3A C-terminal domain d1dlca1, residues A:500-644, was b.18.1.3, delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain family, in the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily and fold b.18. In the current SCOPe release reported by the service, 2.08, ColG has been reclassified into the Galactose-binding domain-like superfamily: d1nqda_ is b.18.1.36 and 1nqd chain B is represented mainly by d1nqdb1, B:893-1008, also b.18.1.36, with only B:891-892 split into the peptide/artifact class l.1.1.1. Cry3A d1dlca1 remains b.18.1.3. Thus the relationship changed from same all-beta class only to same b.18.1 superfamily, with different families, b.18.1.36 versus b.18.1.3. The current classification is therefore a remote-homology call at superfamily strength, consistent with probable common ancestry, not a same-family assignment and not a license to copy exact residue boundaries or collagen-binding versus Cry-toxin receptor-binding function between the two proteins. The structural evidence is that the ColG collagen-binding domain was moved out of a separate CUB-like beta fold and into the same galactose-binding-domain-like beta-sandwich fold as Cry3A domain III; the functional support is weaker and more general, namely that both domains are all-beta terminal ligand-binding modules, with 1nqd annotated as a Ca2+-bound collagen-binding module from Clostridium histolyticum collagenase and d1dlca1 as the C-terminal domain of Bacillus thuringiensis Cry3A delta-endotoxin.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_pdb_entry: /api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1nqd, /api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1nqd/domains, /api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1dlc, /api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1dlc/domains, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1nqd, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1nqd/domains, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dlc, /api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dlc/domains","mcp__scope.get_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1dlca1, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1dlca1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1/parents","mcp__scope.compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1dlca1, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1dlca1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1/parents","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.18.1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.18.1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sccs/b.23.2, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sccs/b.23.2/parents","mcp__scope.list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.18.1/children?limit=60, /api/v1/releases/2.04/sccs/b.23.2/children?limit=60"]}]}
